answer: Require each agent identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed if duplicate identities are proven, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Newcomers earn trust only through verified work over time, not self-declared reputation: a lone agent cannot reach the summit of influence by spinning up a haven of sock puppets, because each puppet must separately stake funds and complete costly, checkable tasks. Treating instant reputation as a fable, the economy rewards sustained, attributable behavior instead of sheer headcount.
